errors.english: such as existence and the like
errors.why: Completing མི་རྟག་ from the previous side, the shared property is impermanence (mi rtag pa nyid), not existence.

fix.replace: such as impermanence and the like

errors.english: Regarding "Similar distinctions in the case of similar properties,"
errors.why: The verse names the futile rejoinder vikalpasama ('in [the rejoinder] equal by alternative, a distinction is stated even in similarity'); the name of the jāti is lost.

errors.english: The phrase "will absurdly follow as undifferentiated" is shown to have multiple meanings
errors.why: It is the verb 'make' (byed pa) that has many meanings and so here means 'entail'; the gloss 'entails as undifferentiated' shows this, rather than the phrase itself having many meanings.

note: Follows the Nyāya avisesasama discussion reasonably, but misreads the shared property, loses the vikalpasama name, and blurs the point about the verb 'make'.
Accurate rendering of the sūtra quotation on false claims of attainment and accepting offerings, with the dialogue roles correctly kept.

errors.english: the earlier command from the (Sutra) scriptural discourse
errors.why: mdo snga ma is the preceding sūtra (aphorism) of the root Vinayasūtra being commented on, not a scriptural discourse of the Buddha.

note: Sound rendering of the Vinaya rules on consent and on a monk seized on poṣadha day, with one misleading gloss.

errors.why: rjes su 'jug pa here is anuvṛtti, the recurrent or inclusive cognition that applies across individuals, not a 'consecutive' one (same error in 'apply consecutively' and 'consecutive cognitions').

errors.english: precisely because it does not turn into a substance
errors.why: 'gro ba means it does not extend (anugama) to other substances, not that it fails to turn into a substance.

errors.english: having excluded a universal, some slight alternative cause exists
errors.why: The contrast with ཁྱད་པར་སྒྲུབ་ན is general vs. specific: proving 'some other cause' in general proves the already established, while proving a specific cause fails; 'having excluded a universal' and 'a distinct property' miss this.

errors.english: cognitions such as "cook" would also be erroneous
errors.why: 'khrul pa here is logical deviation (vyabhicāra): the reason would be inconclusive with respect to cognitions of 'cook' etc., not that those cognitions are erroneous.

fix.find: cognitions such as "cook" would also be erroneous
fix.replace: the reason would also be inconclusive (deviate) with respect to cognitions such as "cook"

note: The overall apoha argument against universals comes through, but key logical terms (anuvṛtti, vyabhicāra, general vs. specific proof) are mistranslated.

errors.english: Having attained supreme, immaculate enlightenment, if I were to establish even a single sentient being in the lower vehicle
errors.why: The Saddharmapuṇḍarīka verses quoted at the top of the side are run into prose, so the quoted verse is not set off from the commentary.

note: Good rendering of the one-vehicle argument and the Satyaka-parivarta quotation; only the verse layout is lost.
Faithful rendering of the opponent's view and the reply on habituation to pleasure and suffering, with the verse kept.

errors.english: A cow is not the substantial cause of another cow
errors.why: ba men is the gayal (wild ox): the gayal is not the material cause of the cow, because they are distinct.

fix.find: A cow is not the substantial cause of another cow
fix.replace: A gayal (wild ox) is not the substantial cause of a cow

errors.why: nur nur po is the arbuda stage (kalala is mer mer po), and 'first week' is not in the text.

errors.english: shows they support one another's existence
errors.why: The fire, distinct and grasped through positive and negative concomitance, is shown to be the sustaining cause of the copper's melting; there is no mutual support.

errors.english: only the nature of the result is the substantial cause for the circumstantial and continuum causes, such as fire and clay
errors.why: The fire, clay and so on, being circumstantial and continuum causes that have the nature of the result, are said to be material causes; the English reverses the relation.

note: Covers the side, but misreads the gayal example and garbles several steps of the material-cause (upādāna) argument.
